title: npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too

review.summary: The migration is small and mostly correct. ai.js never passed temperature, top_p or top_k, uses no Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry client, and sends plain string message content. The only code change is the return statement in askJasmin (ai.js line 39). It now joins every text block instead of reading content[0].text. That avoids returning undefined if the first block under the new API version is not text. The new check stubs globalThis.fetch and confirms three things: the SDK resolves to 1.x, it sends anthropic-version 2026-10-21, and no sampling params are sent. That supports the 'verified' grade for the client side. The check does not prove the live API accepts this request shape and model under 2026-10-21, and it does not prove the production Node runtime supports the new SDK. I could not confirm the 2026-10-21 version or the 1.0.0 package contents from memory. The changelog quote and the SDK's own types/README are where to check. Pre-existing: response.content handling assumes a non-error response, and there is no try/catch around client.messages.create; this is unchanged by the PR.

concerns.issue: Line 39 changes behaviour beyond the forced minimum. Multiple text blocks are now concatenated instead of taking only the first, and a reply with no text blocks returns '' instead of throwing or returning undefined. This is likely an improvement, but callers (e.g. index.js, not shown) that send the reply over Twilio may now send an empty WhatsApp message instead of failing.

The check runs entirely against a stubbed fetch. It never shows that the real API, under version 2026-10-21, accepts model 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514' with string-content history messages, or what response shape it returns. The 'verified' grade covers the client-side request only, not live behaviour.

SDK 1.0.0 drops node-fetch and the polyfills and relies on global fetch, Response and Headers; the test also depends on those globals. No engines field pins a Node version, so a deploy target older than Node 18 would break at runtime. The lockfile also shows the license changing from MIT to Apache-2.0, which is minor but worth noticing.
No npm script runs this file (package.json has no test script), so it only runs in the agent's harness, not in the repo's own CI.

checkFirst: Make one real call with the bumped SDK (staging key) and confirm the API accepts version 2026-10-21 and the claude-sonnet-4-20250514 model.
Confirm the production/hosting Node version is 18+ and has global fetch.
Check how index.js handles an empty-string reply from askJasmin before sending it via Twilio.
Skim the SDK 1.0.0 CHANGELOG/types for MessageParam to confirm plain string content is still accepted for history entries.

review.summary: The PR only bumps @anthropic-ai/sdk from ^0.20.0 to ^1.0.0 (the lock resolves 1.4.0) and changes no application code. The match agent named no call sites, and the diff does not show index.js, which is the entry point and almost certainly calls client.messages.create for the WhatsApp bot. That is a jump from 0.20 to 1.x across two major lines (0.x to 1.0). Per the change description, 1.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default, removes temperature/top_p/top_k, and makes MessageParam a union. Any of these could break index.js at runtime, and because this is plain JS, no type check would catch it. No checks were recorded, not even an install, a require smoke test or a syntax check. needs-review is the right grade; nothing here proves the bot still works. I could not confirm the 1.4.0 version or the new dependencies (@opentelemetry/api, standardwebhooks, json-schema-to-ts) from memory. Check them against the npm registry and the SDK CHANGELOG. The license also changes from MIT to Apache-2.0 in the lockfile, which is worth noting for compliance.

concerns.issue: index.js was not inspected or updated. If it passes temperature, top_p or top_k to messages.create, those parameters are removed in 1.0 and the request may be rejected or the values silently dropped. Response parsing (for example content[0].text) and the error-class or import shape (require('@anthropic-ai/sdk') default vs named export) may also have changed between 0.20 and 1.x.
The new default API version 2026-10-21 can change request and response semantics for the live bot, and the model ID in use may not be valid under it. None of this is exercised by any check.
The caret range ^1.0.0 combined with the lock at 1.4.0 pulls in four minor releases beyond the major bump the change describes, which widens the surface of untested changes.

The SDK license changes from MIT to Apache-2.0 and new runtime dependencies are added (an optional zod peer dependency, the standardwebhooks package, a CLI bin). The new json-schema-to-ts dependency requires Node >=16; check the deploy runtime's Node version.

checkFirst: Open index.js and find every Anthropic client call. Check for temperature, top_p or top_k, how messages are built, and how response.content is read.
Run npm ci and node -e "require('@anthropic-ai/sdk')" to confirm the CommonJS import shape still works in 1.4.0.
Send one real or staging WhatsApp message through the bot under SDK 1.4.0 and confirm the reply is produced.
Read the SDK CHANGELOG from 0.20 through 1.4.0 for the other breaking changes, and confirm the model ID the bot uses is valid under API version 2026-10-21.
